text: Last time, we learned big friend adding.
Take away the friend, then carry to the tens rod.
This video is all about big friend taking away.
First, always look at the ones rod.
If there are enough beads, just take them away.
Now let us try ten take away one.
One bead on the tens rod, and nothing on the ones rod.
How many beads can we take away?
A big friend can help us.
We want to take away one.
So here is the big friend trick for taking away.
Take away one is the same as add nine, then take away ten.
Minus one equals plus nine, minus ten.
Taking away ten takes away too much.
So we add the nine back first.
And we are left with taking away one.
Let us do it on the abacus.
The ones rod goes first, and lower beads move before the upper bead.
First, add nine on the ones rod.
Push four lower beads up, then the upper bead down.
Now the tens rod gets its turn.
Take one bead away from the tens rod.
Ten take away one is nine.
That is our first big friend formula for taking away.
Let us try twelve take away three.
One bead on the tens rod, and two lower beads on the ones rod.
Can we take away three from the ones rod?
There are only two beads there.
So we call a big friend.
Minus three equals plus seven, minus ten.
Push two lower beads up, then the upper bead down.
Now take one bead away from the tens rod.
Twelve take away three is nine!

Now, what about taking away a big number, like seven?
Let us try eleven take away seven.
One bead on the tens rod, and one lower bead on the ones rod.
Can we take away seven from just one bead?
Minus seven equals plus three, minus ten.
Then take one bead away from the tens rod.
Eleven take away seven is four!
The big numbers work the same way.
Every single time, we did the same two things.
Add the friend on the ones rod first.
Then take one bead away from the tens rod.
There is one for every number, from take away one to take away nine.
That is nine big friend formulas for taking away.
One bead on the tens rod, and three lower beads on the ones rod.
Minus nine equals plus one, minus ten.
Add one lower bead on the ones rod, then take one bead away from the tens rod.
Thirteen take away nine is four!
So now you know big friend taking away.
Nine formulas, and they are all yours.
Try them at home on your own abacus.
